explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 42 sits near 1 (mean 0.99) and dips only at D1 (and slightly at GO) in the last ~10 trials of the episode, down to ~0.3-0.5. Beyond the per-decile timing baseline, the dip size is set by the previous trial, scaled by an exponential ramp toward trial 99 (scale 5 trials): it is much deeper when the last trial reached S2 (weight about -0.28 x ramp), deeper again when that was a rare a1->S2 transition (about -0.17 x ramp, plus a small constant -0.02 at D1 throughout the episode), and deeper when the last trial was unrewarded (about -0.06 x ramp); the trial before adds a little (unrewarded lowers, S2 raises). The ramp alone adds only 0.055 test R^2; the history x lateness terms give the rest. D2 is flat at ~1. The belief log-odds adds nothing (tested, R^2 went down slightly), and neither do choice or good-state cues. Observed-only, 8 terms: test R^2 beyond timing 0.49 (dev 0.49), well above the profile additive all ceiling 0.17 (all observed 0.15), which has no within-decile lateness interaction. Using no model outputs costs nothing measurable here: the profile policy decile reference was only 0.05.

issues: Reproduced the score: test R^2 beyond timing is 0.4935 with the 8 terms. The pieces hold up when scored separately on test. The ramp alone gives 0.055. Adding prev S2 x ramp gives 0.334. Adding rare (or a1) S2 x ramp on top gives 0.437, and adding prev unrewarded x ramp instead gives 0.368. So 'S2 drives most of it, rare a1->S2 adds more, unrewarded adds a little' checks out.

The S2 effect really is about the state reached, not about the transition being rare. In the residual table at D1, a2 S2 (common) sits at -0.003 / -0.013, while a2 S1 (rare) is +0.017 / +0.014 and a1 S2 (rare) is -0.037 / -0.042.
The 'only at D1, slightly at GO, D2 flat' claim matches the timing profile. In the last decile the means are D1 0.825, GO 0.978, D2 0.996. In misses, GO and D2 errors stay at or below 0.004.

Minor wording problem: the -0.28 S2 weight is partly cancelled by the +0.099 weight on the plain D1 ramp. The net effect of S2 relative to S1 is about -0.18 x ramp, so the explanation's coefficients are relative, not absolute drops.

Belief adds nothing meaningful, which agrees with the explanation. Swapping belief_lo x ramp in for the trial-before-last reward term scores 0.488 on test, against 0.497 for the reward term. Added to a reduced 5-term set it gives only +0.008.

The ramp shape is slightly mis-specified. The S2 effect speeds up near trial 99: an extra (prev_state==2) x ramp^2 term with scale 6 lifts test R^2 to 0.518 (dev 0.521). This is a small refinement, not a missing class of behaviour.

No large systematic errors remain. Mean errors by phase x previous trial are all within +/-0.009. The remaining ~50% of variance shows up as whole windows that sit low (for example repeated a2 S2c rewarded trials at trials 94-99, with actual 0.55 against predicted 0.72). That looks like episode-specific state that observed variables (belief, cover, counts of recent S2 visits) do not capture.
The 0.17 'ceiling' is an additive table with no lateness interaction, so beating it is expected and is a weak comparison. Still, 0.49 clears the stated >= 0.45 rule.
